description: Media Arts Year 9-10 width tiers — 7 standards, all capability strands. Generated from width_generation_prompt.md v1.0.
subject: Media Arts

width_notes.minimum_width: The narrowest single production or investigative context that honestly meets the descriptor's command term at Y9-10 sophistication.
width_notes.typical_width: Full Y9-10 scope — multiple genres, techniques and contexts engaged; representations designed and analysed with critical awareness of ideology, audience positioning and media conventions.
width_notes.wider: Additional task contexts: different genres, auteur styles, film movements, platforms, distribution contexts, First Nations Australian media arts and identity.
width_notes.elaborations: ACARA elaborations used as source data. First Nations elaborations always represented in wider.

AC9AMA10C01.minimum_width: Design and structure one media arts work that examines and communicates ideas or perspectives — using pre-production processes (shot list, storyboard, screenplay or treatment) and at least two technical elements (camera, sound, editing, mise-en-scène) to construct representations for an intended audience.
AC9AMA10C01.typical_width: Design and structure media arts works across two or more contexts (documentary, genre film, music video, community service announcement, game design, website) that examine social, cultural or identity issues; apply technical and symbolic codes to construct, confirm or challenge stereotypical representations; use pre-production processes to trial, design and refine; experiment with genre hybrids.
wider: Design a media arts work that uses mise-en-scène, camera work, sound and editing typical of a specific genre, auteur or film movement — then design an alternative version that challenges those conventions and compare how each communicates differently to audiences

Create a film trailer or social media campaign that communicates alternative representations of a social group or cultural issue — documenting design decisions and reflecting on how pre-production choices shaped the final representation

Design and structure a media arts work that addresses First Nations Australian perspectives or histories, applying culturally responsive approaches and appropriate protocols — collaborating with community resources to ensure respectful representation
elaborations: using media technologies, languages and representations when designing a media arts work such as a computer game, community service announcement, website or music video
using media technologies to design a media arts work that communicates stereotypical representations for a specific target audience
designing the camera work, sound, editing or mise-en-scène to construct alternative representations of people, places, ideas and events
examining the way technical and symbolic codes and conventions of specific film, television or radio genres have been used in a media arts work

AC9AMA10C02.minimum_width: Apply production processes and media arts concepts to produce one media arts work — using mise-en-scène, camera work, sound, editing and media technologies to construct representations that communicate ideas for a specific audience.
AC9AMA10C02.typical_width: Produce media arts works across multiple forms and contexts (silent film, music video, stop motion, animation, genre film) applying full production processes; collaborate with communities to explore local histories and identities; use genre conventions to confirm or challenge audience expectations; apply ethical, legal and cultural safety considerations throughout production.
wider: Film a short sequence using mise-en-scène and camera angles typical of a genre or film movement — then produce an alternative version that disrupts those conventions, comparing how each positions the audience differently and evaluating which more effectively communicates intended meaning

Collaborate with a local community (including First Nations Australian community contacts, using school protocols) to produce a media arts work that explores, challenges or celebrates local histories, cultures or identities

Create multiple representations of the same person, place or concept in different media forms and for different intentions — evaluating how each medium and audience relationship shapes the representation produced
elaborations: filming a short sequence to show a conflict, and selecting camera angles, lighting and costume to convey meaning through silent film, music video, stop motion or computer animation
collaborating with communities to explore, challenge and celebrate local histories, cultures and identities
using mise-en-scène, camera work, sound, editing and media technologies in ways that are typically used in a genre, auteur or film movement
using Viewpoints to frame questions and evaluate how their intentions are being communicated
creating multiple representations of the same person, place or concept in different media and for different intentions

AC9AMA10D01.minimum_width: Experiment with at least one media arts form — manipulating technical and symbolic codes to construct a representation and reflecting on how the manipulation serves the intended audience relationship.
AC9AMA10D01.typical_width: Experiment with a range of production contexts (music video, short film, documentary, social media product, genre film); research target audiences; manipulate mise-en-scène, camera work, sound and editing in ways typical of a chosen genre or auteur; use design and post-production processes to engage audiences.
wider: Research target audiences and conventions used in successful online media arts works — use findings to design and produce a media arts work that deliberately constructs audience relationships, documenting how research shaped production decisions

Experiment with mise-en-scène, camera work, sound and editing techniques characteristic of a specific genre, auteur or film movement — producing multiple drafts that each prioritise a different technical approach and comparing their effects

Investigate a social media influencer, auteur or game designer's use of technical and symbolic elements to construct representations — apply this analysis to inform original production work that builds on, responds to or challenges their approach
elaborations: examining the way technical and symbolic codes are shaped by a media artist such as a social media influencer, auteur, game designer or music video director
researching target audiences and conventions used in successful online media arts works
experimenting with use of mise-en-scène, camera work, sound, editing and media technologies in ways that are typically used in a genre, auteur or film movement
manipulating technical and symbolic media codes and conventions of specific film, television or radio genres to produce a media arts work for a target audience

AC9AMA10D02.minimum_width: Reflect on at least one production decision made during their own or others' media arts work — documenting a creative choice and explaining how it was informed by analysis of existing works or audience feedback.
AC9AMA10D02.typical_width: Systematically reflect on creative choices throughout production stages; document and explain decisions about representations and genre codes; use Viewpoints questions to examine how camera work, sound, editing and mise-en-scène have been manipulated; use editing software to experiment with structure, filters, text and pace; develop DSLR skills through reflective practice (ISO, shutter speed, aperture).
wider: Use editing software to experiment systematically with structuring sequences — applying filters, text, music, rhythm and pace across multiple versions of the same sequence (e.g. teen flick conventions vs suspense conventions) and comparing how each creates meaning for audiences

Develop DSLR camera skills through reflective practice — documenting experiments with ISO, shutter speed and aperture settings across different lighting conditions and reflecting on how manual control serves the intended meaning of the image

Pay homage to an influential director by manipulating pace and rhythm in a sequence — documenting how the director's approach was analysed, which techniques were applied, and how the resulting work communicates intended meaning
elaborations: developing skills needed to use selected media technologies to produce a photographic sequence, developing understanding through reflective practice of how to use the manual settings for ISO, shutter speed and aperture
identifying and developing knowledge and skills needed to produce a media arts work
using Viewpoints to frame questions and explore possibilities
documenting and explaining their creative choices in relation to representations or genre codes and conventions
using editing software to experiment with structuring sequences
using Viewpoints to develop investigating questions when making decisions about how they will represent a theme, concept or idea

AC9AMA10E01.minimum_width: Investigate how media artists use media arts concepts to construct representations in at least one context — analysing how technical and symbolic codes communicate values, themes or ideas to specific audiences.
AC9AMA10E01.typical_width: Investigate media arts works across cultures, times and contexts; analyse and evaluate how social beliefs and values are communicated through technical and symbolic codes; examine stereotypical representations across historical and contemporary media; evaluate how media platforms use data to influence audience information; research audiences of specific genres and analyse how codes engage them.
wider: Analyse and evaluate the social, cultural and/or ethical implications of changing representations in media arts works over time — for example, deconstructing representations of gender or multiculturalism in Australian television across decades and evaluating the social forces shaping each period

Research how media platforms use data to influence the breadth and depth of information provided to audiences — investigating algorithmic curation through media feeds and evaluating the implications for audience agency and representation

Justify, in a video commentary, the technical and symbolic code choices made in constructing representations — explaining the social and cultural value framework behind choices and communicating alternative points of view
elaborations: analysing and evaluating the social, cultural and/or ethical implications of the changing nature of representations in media arts works over time
justifying, in a video commentary, the technical and symbolic code choices they have made in constructing representations
analysing and evaluating the way social beliefs and values can be communicated to audiences through the manipulation of technical and symbolic codes
exploring how media platforms use data and how they can influence the breadth and depth of information provided to an audience
evaluating relationships embedded within media practices
researching audiences of specific genres or users of specific media platforms
analysing and evaluating the ways technical and symbolic codes have been used to construct stereotypical representations
identifying, describing and explaining the way technical and symbolic codes are manipulated to evoke audience responses
examining the role of media makers in perpetuating and/or challenging prevailing views

AC9AMA10E02.minimum_width: Investigate at least one way First Nations Australian media artists and/or producers celebrate and/or challenge perspectives of Australian identity — identifying how media arts practices are used to communicate ideas, messages or lived experiences.
AC9AMA10E02.typical_width: Investigate how First Nations Australian media artists explore and challenge concepts and histories of Australian identity; compare and critique multiple practitioners' use of media arts to celebrate and challenge perspectives; examine how media arts provide a voice through film, television and online platforms; analyse how music videos, feature films, CSAs, advertisements and news reports depict First Nations Australians' histories and cultures.
wider: Compare and critique the work of multiple First Nations Australian media artists or producers — examining how each uses their practice to communicate multiple ways of understanding an issue such as land rights, family, stereotyping or dispossession, and evaluating the potential impact on community debate and audience perception

Analyse how First Nations Australians are represented across different media institutions and forms (film, television, online platforms) — evaluating how these representations have changed over time and what forces have driven those changes

Investigate how First Nations Australian media arts works challenge community debate and present multiple perspectives on caring for Country/Place — analysing specific case studies and evaluating their impact on audience understanding
elaborations: investigating how First Nations Australian media artists and/or producers are exploring and challenging concepts and histories of Australia and Australian identity
exploring the ways that First Nations Australian media artists and/or producers use their practice to communicate ideas, messages and lived experiences to the broader community
comparing and critiquing ways First Nations Australian media artists use their practice to celebrate and challenge perspectives about Australia's identity
using questions based on Viewpoints to examine the ideology or philosophical stance taken in media arts works
understanding the ways that media arts provide a voice for First Nations Australians through media institutions and forms
analysing the ways that First Nations Australian media artists use their practice to challenge and inform community debate

AC9AMA10P01.minimum_width: Present a media arts work to an audience and apply at least two responsible media practices — including appropriate rights, permissions and consideration of audience relationships in the distribution context chosen.
AC9AMA10P01.typical_width: Present and distribute media arts works to audiences via personal, community and/or institutional contexts; investigate classification systems and their impact on producers and users; apply copyright, Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property rights, and online safety protocols; produce guidelines for appropriate online conduct; plan and evaluate audience relationships created by specific distribution choices.
wider: Distribute a media arts work via an online platform (school LMS) — applying appropriate rights and permissions, producing guidelines for ethical online conduct, and alerting audiences to issues of appropriation and First Nations Australian ICIP rights; evaluate the audience relationships created

Investigate Australia's classification system for different media platforms — analysing the impact on producers and audiences, and applying classification thinking to decisions made during their own production and distribution process

Research differences between government regulation and self-regulation in media production and distribution — comparing how different media producers (sole digital producers, multi-platform, cross-media organisations, public and private sector) develop relationships with audiences, and applying findings to plan distribution of their own work
elaborations: investigating differences between government regulation and self-regulation
researching Australia's classification system for various media platforms
distributing a media arts work they have produced via an online platform, using appropriate rights and permissions; producing a set of guidelines for appropriate online conduct
using media technologies to design and produce a media arts work that promotes a community event
investigating the relationships created between intended audiences and the media arts works they create
